body.html: RP City Hotel is a small hotel right in central Yasothon, on Prachasampan Road in the shopping district — only about 0.5 km from the city center. Its appeal isn't luxury; it's the basics travelers actually want: clean rooms, hot water that works, easy parking, and a location that puts you a short drive from everything.

Rooms are simple but cover what matters — king bed, flat-screen TV, fridge, hot shower and free Wi-Fi in every room. Reviews agree the housekeeping is solid, linens are fresh, and the hot water comes through fast and steady, which is exactly where same-price provincial hotels often fall short. The deluxe rooms are larger and add a sofa, handy if you're staying a few nights or want a corner to work.
"Clean room, good hot water, friendly staff, and very cheap for what you get — and in the evening there's a restaurant with live music."

What sets RP City apart from hotels at the same price is the on-site restaurant with live music in the evening. There's a relaxed seating area by the ground-floor lobby, a front garden to sit in, and a small fitness room downstairs. Breakfast is a simple Thai set, included in some packages. None of it is fancy, but it's an easy, comfortable vibe that makes a night in Yasothon feel more relaxed than just crashing for sleep.

Location is the real edge here — it's about a 5-minute walk to the Toad Museum (Phaya Khan Khak) and roughly the same to the historic Ban Singha Tha old quarter. Phaya Thaen Park and the river are a short drive away. During the Yasothon Rocket Festival (Bun Bang Fai, in May) this spot is ideal for watching the processions, so rooms fill fast. Outside festival season the town is fairly quiet, which many guests count as a plus if you actually want to rest.

To be straight with you, RP City Hotel isn't for everyone. The limitation reviewers flag is no elevator — if you land an upper-floor room, you'll be carrying bags up the stairs. The building and furnishings look plain and show their age; this is not a sleek new design hotel. And if you expect a spa, a pool or upscale service, you won't find it here. But if the brief is a clean, well-priced, central place to sleep, this delivers it in full and the value is real.

In short, RP City Hotel suits road-trippers, business travelers and people heading home who want a clean, affordable central room. Real guest reviews consistently score it high for value and cleanliness. If you're booking around the Rocket Festival, reserve several weeks ahead, and if you're hauling heavy luggage, ask for a ground-floor room when you book.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — RP City Hotel Yasothon

faq.q: Where is RP City Hotel in Yasothon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: RP City Hotel is at 275 Prachasampan Road, Nai Mueang, in central Yasothon's shopping district, about 0.5 km from the city center. It's a short walk to the Toad Museum and the historic Ban Singha Tha old quarter, with Phaya Thaen Park and Phra That Kong Khao Noi a quick drive away.

faq.q: What does RP City Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿900/night for a Standard room with a king bed. Larger Superior and Deluxe rooms run roughly ฿1,100–฿1,350. Prices depend on dates and availability — they rise and sell out fast around the Rocket Festival, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does RP City Hotel have an elevator? Is it suitable for seniors or heavy luggage?
faq.a: There is no elevator, so upper-floor rooms mean stairs. If you're traveling with older guests, carrying heavy bags, or have trouble with stairs, ask for a ground-floor room when you book or at the front desk before check-in.

faq.q: Who is RP City Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for road-trippers, business travelers and people heading home who want a clean, affordable central room. Real reviews consistently praise the value and cleanliness. It's less suited to anyone wanting a pool, spa or a brand-new design hotel.

faq.q: Does RP City Hotel have a restaurant and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. The on-site restaurant opens in the evening with live music, and there's large free parking out front. There's also a front garden and a small downstairs fitness room, plus a simple Thai breakfast set included in some packages.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: In normal periods, 1–2 weeks ahead is fine. But for the Yasothon Rocket Festival (May), book several weeks ahead — the central location means rooms go quickly. Choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm yet.
